name: Isolation Traverse
blurb: Multi-day North Cascades ski traverse from Eldorado over the Inspiration and McAllister glaciers and Backbone Ridge, past Isolation Peak to Pyramid Lake.

name: Magic S Loop
blurb: Spring ski loop from Cascade Pass: Cache Col, Kool-Aid Lake, Hurry-up Peak, down the S and Yawning glaciers and back. First done in 2007.

name: Summit at Snoqualmie
blurb: Ski resort right off I-90 at Snoqualmie Pass, about an hour from Seattle; Summit West is its beginner-friendly, night-skiing hub.

name: Alpental
blurb: Steep ski area on the north side of Snoqualmie Pass beneath Denny Mountain; its backcountry gate opens into the Alpental Valley.

name: Mount Washington (Oregon)
blurb: Deeply eroded volcano between Three Fingered Jack and the Three Sisters, its summit a sharp lava plug above Santiam Pass.

name: Mount McLoughlin
blurb: Symmetrical 9,495 ft cone near Medford, the highest peak in southern Oregon's Cascades; a long trail reaches its summit.

name: Newberry Volcano
blurb: Vast shield volcano south of Bend whose caldera holds Paulina and East lakes and the Big Obsidian Flow. Pin is Paulina Peak.

name: Mount Meager
blurb: Volcanic massif northwest of Pemberton; in 2010 Capricorn Mountain's flank collapsed in one of Canada's largest recorded landslides.

name: Mount Cayley
blurb: Crumbling, spire-studded volcano west of the Squamish River, part of the Garibaldi Volcanic Belt north of Squamish.

name: Mount Edziza
blurb: Huge volcanic complex in northern BC's Stikine country, ringed by cinder cones and lava fields in its own provincial park.

name: Black Tusk
blurb: Jagged volcanic neck in Garibaldi Park, visible from the Sea-to-Sky Highway; the loose final chimney scramble is a local rite.

name: Mount Price
blurb: Small volcano on the west shore of Garibaldi Lake; lava from its Clinker Peak vent built The Barrier that dams the lake.

name: Camp Muir
blurb: Stone-hut high camp at about 10,000 ft on Rainier, top of the Muir Snowfield ski run and base for the Disappointment Cleaver route.

name: Paradise
blurb: Rainier's south-side visitor area and one of the snowiest measured places on Earth; start of the Skyline Trail and Muir Snowfield.

name: Artist Point
blurb: End of the Mt Baker Highway between Baker and Shuksan; the jumping-off point for Table Mountain and Ptarmigan Ridge.

name: Shuksan Arm
blurb: Ridge running west from Mt Shuksan toward the Mt Baker Ski Area, a sidecountry classic reached through the resort's backcountry gate.

name: Mt Herman
blurb: Peak just north of the Mt Baker Ski Area, popular for quick backcountry laps with big views of Shuksan.

name: Ruth Mountain
blurb: Glaciated peak above Hannegan Pass east of Shuksan; a favorite first glacier climb and spring ski with a close-up view of Shuksan.

name: Coleman-Deming Route
blurb: Mt Baker's standard route from the Heliotrope Ridge trail: up the Coleman Glacier to the saddle, then the Roman Wall to Grant Peak.

name: Easton Glacier
blurb: Mt Baker's south-side glacier, approached via the Railroad Grade moraine; a popular route for climbing and skiing the peak.

name: Chair Peak
blurb: Striking pyramid above Source Lake near Alpental; its northeast buttress is a Snoqualmie Pass winter-climbing classic.

name: Snoqualmie Mountain
blurb: Highest peak above Alpental, with steep backcountry couloirs in winter and a relentless summer scramble trail from the Alpental road.

name: Red Mountain (Snoqualmie)
blurb: Rust-colored peak north of Snoqualmie Pass above Commonwealth Basin, a popular steep backcountry ski objective.

name: Granite Mountain
blurb: Lookout-topped peak on I-90 west of Snoqualmie Pass; its steep south-facing trail crosses a notorious winter avalanche path.

name: Jove Peak
blurb: Peak northeast of Stevens Pass whose open bowls are a go-to backcountry tour starting near the old Yodelin ski area.

name: Skyline Lake
blurb: Small lake just north of Stevens Pass, the quickest backcountry tour from the pass up toward Skyline Ridge.

name: Birthday Tour
blurb: Washington Pass spring classic: skin past Blue Lake under Liberty Bell, ski Madison Avenue into Copper Creek, exit at the SR-20 hairpin.

name: Cutthroat Peak
blurb: Rugged granite peak just west of Washington Pass above SR-20, known for alpine rock routes and spring ski couloirs.

name: Silver Star Mountain
blurb: Big granite peak east of Washington Pass; the Silver Star Glacier and Burgundy Col make a classic spring ski descent.

name: Naches Peak
blurb: Peak at Chinook Pass circled by a short loop trail famous for wildflowers and Rainier views; a spring tour when SR-410 opens.

name: White Pass Ski Area
blurb: Ski area on US-12 southeast of Mt Rainier, the home hill where Olympic racers Phil and Steve Mahre grew up.

name: Mission Ridge
blurb: Dry east-slope ski area above Wenatchee; wreckage from a 1944 B-24 bomber crash still sits on its slopes.

name: Hurricane Hill
blurb: End of the road past Hurricane Ridge in Olympic NP; a short paved trail climbs to views of Mt Olympus and the Strait.

name: Mt Pilchuck
blurb: Lookout-capped peak near Granite Falls that hosted a ski area until 1980; now one of the busiest hikes off the Mountain Loop.

name: Mt Adams South Spur
blurb: Adams' non-technical standard route from Cold Springs: up to the Lunch Counter, over the Piker's Peak false summit, on to the top.

name: Worm Flows
blurb: Mt St Helens' winter route from Marble Mountain Sno-Park, up lava-flow ridges past Chocolate Falls to the crater rim.
